t: The battle brought the Maratha Empire, whose rule had reached north of the Indus in 1758, into direct conflict with the Durrani Empire, which the Marathas' hold on Punjab and Delhi had threatened.
The Marathas were besieged for about two months in their lines, and Sadashivrao Bhau led them out on 13 January because supplies had run short.
The killing did not end with the fighting: the best eyewitness chronicle reports about 40,000 prisoners killed the day after, and about 22,000 women and children were taken as slaves.
dyk: The battle perhaps had the largest number of fatalities in a single day reported in a classic formation battle between two armies, and the Marathas brought roughly 200,000 non-combatants, among them pilgrims, with their army.
ev: The Marathas take Lahore with Adina Beg Khan and drive out Timur Shah Durrani, extending their rule north of the Indus
Ahmad Shah Durrani raises an army and wins over Najib-ud-Daula, the Rohillas and Shuja-ud-Daula
The Maratha army under Sadashivrao Bhau starts north from Patdur
The Afghans cross the Yamuna at Baghpat and skirmish at Samalkha, which leaves the Marathas partly encircled
The Marathas leave their camp before dawn on 13 January and face the Afghan lines at about eight in the morning
The main battle is fought on 14 January; Vishwasrao is killed and the Maratha lines break
Prisoners are killed the day after the battle and women and children are driven off as slaves
Ahmad Shah leaves for Afghanistan, with the Sikhs harassing his march through Punjab

f.date: 14 January 1761, after skirmishing and a siege of about two months
f.place: In and around the city of Panipat, about 97 kilometres (60 mi) north of Delhi, in present-day India
f.sides: The Maratha Empire under Sadashivrao Bhau, with an army put at between 45,000 and 60,000 and roughly 200,000 non-combatants; the Durrani Empire under Ahmad Shah Durrani (Abdali), with Najib-ud-Daula, the Rohillas and Shuja-ud-Daula of Oudh. Over 125,000 troops are given for the whole battle.
f.outcome: The Afghan army won after several Maratha flanks were destroyed. Between 60,000 and 70,000 troops are believed to have been killed in the fighting, and about 40,000 Maratha prisoners were killed the next day according to an eyewitness chronicle.
